# What Postman API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from ordered characters, which no real credential is.
# A body is two runs of exact length — twenty-four and thirty-four — divided by
# a hyphen neither run may carry, so with the prefix in front a key comes to
# sixty-four. The key the cases are written around carries the run
# 0123456789abcdef and eight characters more, then that run twice over and two
# more; the two cases about the alphabet carry the same ordered characters
# spelled on past f, or spelled uppercase instead.

patterns: postman-api-key

# A key as it is written: the header the Postman API reads it from, the
# environment the tooling takes it out of, the command line it is passed on and
# the body of a request that carries it.

case:     a key in the api key header
in:       X-API-Key: PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      X-API-Key: «postman-api-key»

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       POSTMAN_API_KEY=PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      POSTMAN_API_KEY=«postman-api-key»

case:     a key on a curl command line
in:       curl -H "X-API-Key: PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01" https://api.getpostman.com/me
out:      curl -H "X-API-Key: «postman-api-key»" https://api.getpostman.com/me

case:     a key in a json body
in:       {"apiKey":"PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01"}
out:      {"apiKey":"«postman-api-key»"}

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01.
out:      the key is «postman-api-key».

# The body: the letters of both cases and the digits in both segments, which is
# the wider of the two alphabets the rulesets that read this format divide on.
# Postman publishes no expression of its own, so a key carrying a letter past f
# is one nothing rules out, and reading hexadecimal alone would leave it in the
# output whole. The counts are read exactly rather than as floors, so a run
# longer than the second is a key and what was written after it.

case:     an uppercase body
in:       PMAK-0123456789ABCDEF01234567-0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF01
out:      «postman-api-key»

case:     a body carrying letters past f
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdefghijklmn-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwx
out:      «postman-api-key»

case:     a second segment one character longer is a key and the character after it
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012
out:      «postman-api-key»2

# What a key may be written against: no boundary on either side of the prefix,
# so a key keeps its span whatever character it abuts and what stands past its
# last character stays where it was written.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       POSTMAN_API_KEY_PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      POSTMAN_API_KEY_«postman-api-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xPMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      x«postman-api-key»

case:     a word written against a key
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01suffix
out:      «postman-api-key»suffix

# Keys written together, and the key written inside another. The alphabet a body
# is drawn from holds every letter the prefix opens with, so a second segment may
# close on PMAK and the hyphen reading it back then stands past the end of the
# key that segment closes. That is why the scan resumes a byte past the start of
# a candidate rather than past the candidate, and the third case here is what a
# scan stepping over what it found would lose: the spans overlap and are redacted
# as one.

case:     two keys with nothing between them
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      «postman-api-key»«postman-api-key»

case:     two keys separated by a space
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01 PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      «postman-api-key» «postman-api-key»

case:     a key beginning four characters from the end of another
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdPMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      «postman-api-key»

case:     a prefix in front of a key
in:       PMAK-PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      PMAK-«postman-api-key»

case:     a first segment closing on PMAK, whose candidate borrows the key's own separator
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdef0123PMAK-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      «postman-api-key»

# And what this pattern leaves alone. First the prefix: the case Postman writes
# it in and the hyphen it closes with. Then the body, where a segment of the
# wrong length or a separator written as anything else ends the reading — a run
# of one alphabet all the way through is not a key however long it runs, so no
# digest reaches this format and no UUID does either. Then the collection access
# key, which Postman calls by another name and writes behind another prefix.
# Then the prose and the log line, which no pattern here has anything to find in.

case:     a lowercase prefix
in:       pmak-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      pmak-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     the prefix without its closing hyphen
in:       PMAK0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      PMAK0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     a first segment one character short
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdef0123456-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      PMAK-0123456789abcdef0123456-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     a second segment one character short
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0
out:      PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0

case:     the two segments written with no separator between them
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdef012345670123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      PMAK-0123456789abcdef012345670123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     an underscore where the separator stands
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     a dot in the second segment
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef.123456789abcdef01
out:      PMAK-0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef.123456789abcdef01

case:     a sha-256 digest behind the prefix
in:       PMAK-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      PMAK-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a uuid behind the prefix
in:       PMAK-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      PMAK-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     a body of the right shape with no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      0123456789abcdef01234567-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     a collection access key
in:       PMAT-0123456789abcdef0123456789
out:      PMAT-0123456789abcdef0123456789

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a log line
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.getpostman.com/me
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.getpostman.com/me
